title: Les adjectifs : accord et place
ruleNote: French adjectives describe nouns, but they also obey two rules. First, agreement: the adjective changes form to match its noun's gender and number. Second, placement: most adjectives follow the noun, but a small set of short, common ones (size, age, beauty, goodness) come before it. This module drills both, including the tricky irregulars beau, vieux, and nouveau.

elements.label: L'adjectif s'accorde
elements.ruleNote: A French adjective changes to match its noun's gender and number. 'grand' describes the noun and adapts to it.

examples.explanationEN: "chien" is masculine singular, so it takes "grand".
"maison" is feminine, so it takes "grande".

spot.explanation: « maison » est féminin : on dit « une grande maison ».
spot.explanationEN: "maison" is feminine, so the article is "une".

examples.explanationEN: "chat" is masculine, so it takes "petit".
"ami" is masculine, so it takes "grand".
"amie" is feminine, so it takes "grande".

elements.label: Féminin : + e (grand → grande)
elements.ruleNote: Make most adjectives feminine by adding -e: grand → grande, petit → petite. You often hear the final consonant return.

examples.explanationEN: "table" is feminine, so it takes "petite".
"pomme" is feminine, so it takes "verte".
"ville" is feminine, so it takes "grande".
"voiture" is feminine, so it takes "verte".
"fille" is feminine, so it takes "petite".

elements.label: Adjectifs déjà en -e
elements.ruleNote: Adjectives already ending in -e don't change for the feminine: rouge, jaune, simple stay the same — un livre rouge, une voiture rouge.

examples.explanation: « rouge » finit déjà par -e : pas de changement.
examples.explanationEN: "rouge" already ends in -e, so there is no change.

examples.explanation: « rouge » ne change pas au féminin.
examples.hint: rouge is the same for both genders.
examples.explanationEN: "rouge" does not change in the feminine.

examples.explanation: « jaune » finit par -e : invariable en genre.
examples.explanationEN: "jaune" ends in -e, so it is invariable in gender.

examples.explanation: « rouge » est déjà en -e → pas de -e en plus.
examples.explanationEN: "rouge" already ends in -e, so there is no extra -e.
"simple" ends in -e, so it keeps the same form.

elements.label: Pluriel : + s (grand → grands)
elements.ruleNote: Make most adjectives plural by adding -s: grands, petites. The -s is usually silent, just like with nouns.

examples.explanationEN: It is plural, so it takes "grands".
It is plural, so it takes "petits".
It is feminine plural, so it takes "vertes".
It is plural, so it takes "rouges".
It is feminine plural, so it takes "petites".

elements.label: Les quatre formes
elements.ruleNote: Each adjective has up to four forms: grand, grande, grands, grandes — masculine/feminine × singular/plural. Match all of them to the noun.

examples.explanationEN: Masculine singular, so it takes "grand".
Feminine singular, so it takes "grande".
Masculine plural, so it takes "grands".
Feminine plural, so it takes "grandes".
Feminine plural, so it takes "petites".

elements.label: Féminin irrégulier : -eux → -euse
elements.ruleNote: Adjectives in -eux become -euse in the feminine: heureux → heureuse. A common pattern worth memorising.

examples.explanationEN: The subject is feminine, so it takes "heureuse".
The subject is masculine, so it takes "heureux".
It is feminine, so it takes "heureuse".
It is masculine, so it takes "heureux".
"fille" is feminine, so it takes "heureuse".

elements.label: Féminin irrégulier : doublement (-on → -onne)
elements.ruleNote: Some adjectives double the consonant before -e: bon → bonne, gentil → gentille. The doubled letter makes the consonant heard.

examples.explanationEN: "idée" is feminine, so it takes "bonne".
"café" is masculine, so it takes "bon".
It is feminine, so it takes "bonne".
It is feminine, so it takes "gentille".
"garçon" is masculine, so it takes "gentil".

elements.label: Adjectif après le nom (couleur)
elements.ruleNote: Most adjectives, including colours, come after the noun: une voiture rouge, un chien noir. This is the default position.

examples.explanation: La couleur vient après le nom.
examples.explanationEN: The colour comes after the noun.
"noir" comes after "chien".
The colour follows the noun.

examples.prompt: Choisis l'ordre correct : un livre noir / un noir livre
examples.explanation: La couleur vient après le nom.
examples.explanationEN: The colour comes after the noun.

examples.prompt: Choisis l'ordre correct : une noire voiture / une voiture noire
examples.explanation: La couleur vient après le nom.
examples.explanationEN: The colour comes after the noun.

elements.label: Adjectifs BAGS avant le nom
elements.ruleNote: A small set goes before the noun — Beauty, Age, Goodness, Size: un grand chien, une petite maison, un bon café.

examples.explanationEN: "grand" comes before the noun.
"petite" comes before the noun.
"bon" comes before the noun.

examples.prompt: Choisis l'ordre : un grand parc / un parc grand
examples.explanationEN: "grand" (size) comes before the noun.

examples.prompt: Choisis l'ordre : une bonne idée / une idée bonne
examples.explanationEN: "bon" comes before the noun.

elements.label: petit / grand (place avant)
elements.ruleNote: Size words 'petit' and 'grand' come before the noun: un petit chat, une grande table. They still agree with the noun.

examples.explanationEN: "petit" comes before the noun and agrees with it.
"grande" comes before the feminine noun.
"petite" comes before the feminine noun.
It is feminine, so it takes "grande", before the noun.
It is masculine, so it takes "grand", before the noun.

elements.label: bon / mauvais (place avant)
elements.ruleNote: Quality words 'bon' and 'mauvais' also precede the noun: un bon livre, une mauvaise idée. Bon → bonne in the feminine.

examples.explanationEN: "bon" comes before the noun.
"mauvaise" comes before the feminine noun.
It is feminine, so it takes "bonne", before the noun.
It is masculine, so it takes "bon".
It is feminine, so it takes "mauvaise".

elements.label: jeune / vieux (l'âge, place avant)
elements.ruleNote: Age adjectives go before: un jeune homme, une vieille maison. 'vieux' has a special feminine, 'vieille'.

examples.explanationEN: "jeune" comes before the noun.

examples.hint: jeune is the same for both genders.
examples.explanationEN: "jeune" is invariable in gender.
It is feminine, so it takes "vieille".
Masculine before a consonant, so it takes "vieux".
It is feminine, so it takes "vieille".

elements.label: beau / belle
elements.ruleNote: 'beau' (beautiful) goes before the noun and has an irregular feminine 'belle': un beau parc, une belle voiture.

examples.explanationEN: "beau" before a masculine noun (consonant).
It is feminine, so it takes "belle".
It is feminine, so it takes "belle".
Masculine before a consonant, so it takes "beau".
It is feminine, so it takes "belle".

elements.label: beau → bel devant une voyelle
elements.ruleNote: Before a masculine noun starting with a vowel, 'beau' becomes 'bel': un bel ami, un bel arbre. It keeps the smooth sound.

examples.explanationEN: Before a vowel, it takes "bel".

examples.explanation: « arbre » commence par une voyelle → « bel ».
examples.explanationEN: "arbre" begins with a vowel, so it takes "bel".
"homme" (mute h), so it takes "bel".
Before a vowel, it takes "bel".
Before a consonant, it takes "beau".

elements.label: vieux / vieil / vieille
elements.ruleNote: 'vieux' (old) becomes 'vieil' before a vowel and 'vieille' in the feminine: un vieux livre, un vieil ami, une vieille amie.

examples.explanationEN: Masculine before a consonant, so it takes "vieux".
Before a vowel, it takes "vieil".
It is feminine, so it takes "vieille".
Before a vowel (mute h), it takes "vieil".
It is feminine, so it takes "vieille".

elements.label: nouveau / nouvel / nouvelle
elements.ruleNote: 'nouveau' (new) follows the same pattern: un nouveau café, un nouvel ami, une nouvelle voiture.

examples.explanationEN: Masculine before a consonant, so it takes "nouveau".
Before a vowel, it takes "nouvel".
It is feminine, so it takes "nouvelle".
Before a consonant, it takes "nouveau".
It is feminine, so it takes "nouvelle".

elements.label: Adjectif avec être
elements.ruleNote: When the adjective comes after être it still agrees with the subject: elle est grande, ils sont contents.

examples.explanationEN: The subject is feminine singular, so it takes "grande".
The subject is masculine singular, so it takes "grand".
The subject is masculine plural, so it takes "contents".
The subject is feminine, so it takes "grande".
The subject is feminine plural, so it takes "contentes".

elements.label: Deux adjectifs (avant et après)
elements.ruleNote: You can use one before and one after: 'un petit chien noir'. Each keeps its normal position and both agree with the noun.

examples.explanationEN: Size before the noun, colour after.
"grande" before the noun, "rouge" after.
"belle" before the noun, "verte" after.

examples.prompt: Choisis l'ordre : un noir petit chat / un petit chat noir
examples.explanationEN: Size before the noun, colour after.

examples.prompt: Choisis l'ordre : une rouge grande table / une grande table rouge
examples.explanationEN: Size before the noun, colour after.

elements.label: Choisir la bonne place
elements.ruleNote: Decide: is it a short BAGS adjective (before) or a normal descriptive one like a colour (after)? Position changes the word order, not the meaning.

examples.prompt: Choisis l'ordre : un grand chien / un chien grand
examples.explanationEN: "grand" (size) comes before the noun.

examples.prompt: Choisis l'ordre : une voiture verte / une verte voiture
examples.explanationEN: The colour comes after the noun.

examples.prompt: Choisis l'ordre : un bon livre / un livre bon
examples.explanationEN: "bon" comes before the noun.

examples.explanation: La couleur vient après le nom.
examples.explanationEN: The colour comes after the noun.
"petite" (size) comes before the noun.

elements.label: Synthèse : accord et place
elements.ruleNote: Put it together: choose the right form for gender and number, and place the adjective before or after the noun correctly.

examples.explanationEN: "belle" before the noun, "rouge" after, feminine.

spot.explanation: « voiture » est féminin : on dit « une belle voiture rouge ».
spot.explanationEN: "voiture" is feminine, so the article is "une".

examples.explanation: Féminin pluriel : « grandes » avant, « vertes » après.
examples.explanationEN: Feminine plural: "grandes" before the noun, "vertes" after.
It is feminine, so it takes "nouvelle", before the noun.

spot.explanation: « amie » est féminin : on dit « une nouvelle amie ».
spot.explanationEN: "amie" is feminine, so the article is "une".

examples.explanationEN: Before a vowel, it takes "vieil".

examples.prompt: Choisis l'ordre : une petite maison blanche / une blanche petite maison
examples.explanationEN: Size before the noun, colour after.
